title: Combination Sum

statement.hi:
**Distinct** integers ka array `candidates` aur ek `target` diya hai. Aise saare **unique combinations** return karo jinka sum `target` ho. Ek hi number ko **kitni bhi baar** le sakte ho.

Do combinations alag tab hain jab kisi number ki frequency alag ho. Combinations (aur unke andar ke numbers) kisi bhi order me ho sakte hain.
statement.en:
Given an array of **distinct** integers `candidates` and a `target`, return all **unique combinations** of `candidates` that sum to `target`. The same number may be chosen an **unlimited** number of times.

Two combinations are different if the frequency of at least one number differs. Combinations (and the numbers inside them) may be in any order.

constraints: All elements of candidates are distinct
The answer has fewer than 150 combinations

hi: Duplicates se bachne ke liye combination ko non-decreasing order me banao: recursion me ek `start` index pass karo.
Same element dobara lene ke liye recurse `i` se karo, `i + 1` se nahi.
Candidates sort karo; jab `candidates[i] > remaining` ho, loop tod do.
en: To avoid duplicates, build each combination in non-decreasing order: pass a `start` index into the recursion.
To reuse the same element, recurse from `i`, not `i + 1`.
Sort the candidates and break once `candidates[i] > remaining`.

explain.hi: 2 + 2 + 3 = 7 aur 7 = 7. Bas yahi do combinations hain.
explain.en: 2 + 2 + 3 = 7 and 7 = 7. These are the only two combinations.

approach.hi:
Candidates sort karo. `dfs(start, remaining)`: `remaining == 0` pe combination save karo; warna `i = start..` har candidate lo aur `dfs(i, remaining - c[i])` call karo (same `i` → reuse allowed). `c[i] > remaining` pe break.
`start` index ki wajah se har combination sirf ek order me banta hai, isliye duplicates nahi aate. Time output size pe depend karta hai (exponential worst case).
approach.en:
Sort the candidates. `dfs(start, remaining)`: when `remaining == 0` save the combination; otherwise for `i = start..` take candidate `i` and call `dfs(i, remaining - c[i])` (same `i` → reuse allowed). Break when `c[i] > remaining`.
The `start` index builds every combination in exactly one order, so no duplicates appear. Time depends on the output size (exponential in the worst case).
